patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: The other driver was texting, and I want that noted. My lower back hurts after the crash, but I can move both legs. And no, I am not putting on one of those paper gowns.
presentation.triageNote: 61-year-old woman with lower-back pain after a motor-vehicle collision. She has midline lumbar tenderness, rates the pain 7 of 10, and is moving both legs.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 3 is appropriate because the patient is stable but is expected to require more than one resource for traumatic spinal assessment and symptom control.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This is a stable older adult with traumatic midline back tenderness who is expected to need multiple resources to exclude spinal injury and control pain.
clinical.acuityReason: She is hemodynamically stable and moving both legs, with no presented sign of immediate instability. Her age, collision mechanism, midline tenderness, and pain still make a simple low-resource strain evaluation inappropriate.
redFlags: Traumatic midline spinal tenderness in an older adult
teachingPoints: Normal leg movement is reassuring but does not exclude a vertebral injury.
A stable presentation can still require imaging, medication, and repeated assessment.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Spinal imaging and repeat neurologic assessment would guide care; stable imaging and controlled pain could allow discharge, while a fracture or neurologic change could require immobilization and specialty evaluation.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.who: well-dressed woman about 60, smart blouse and slacks, tasteful jewelry, hair neatly done
aiImageGeneration.pose: standing beside the clinic chair, leaning forward, one hand gripping the edge of the chair for support
aiImageGeneration.expression: face tight with pain, dignified but clearly hurting
signs: antalgic posture — bent forward, bracing on the chair
other hand pressed to her lower back
aiImageGeneration.lookSeverity: alert and composed, but in real pain and unable to sit comfortably
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a well-dressed Hispanic woman about 60 in a smart blouse and slacks with tasteful jewelry and neat hair, standing beside a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: standing beside the chair, leaning forward, one hand gripping the chair edge for support, the other pressed to her lower back. Expression: only mildly uncomfortable, a slight wince, dignified and composed (NOT in agony, NOT crying). Clearly visible: an antalgic bent-forward posture bracing on the chair. Overall alert, composed, and only moderately uncomfortable - a stiff sore back, not a crisis. No text, no logos.
